record.text: Bounded reading of the captured Pension Credit severe-disability additional-amount rules for a claimant who has a partner. DMG 78045–78047 set distinct lower-rate branches, and 78048–78050 address the higher rate. Their benefit, residence and caring conditions must be read together. DMG 78047's patient branch concerns the other partner being unable to receive the specified benefit because of being a patient for over 28 days; its remaining conditions continue on the next page. DMG 78050 restricts the higher-rate condition when either partner is treated as receiving benefit under the partner-patient provision in 78060(2), and directs consideration of the lower rate. It does not exclude every form of treated receipt. Read the separate CA/UC actual-payment qualification in 78057, in respect of caring for the claimant or partner, and the complete treated-receipt provisions in 78060, with the dated changes in memos 02/25, 06/25 and 01/26. This component does not establish that partner status persists after care-home admission, consolidate current law or calculate an award.

record.text:
77123 Substantially has no specific legal meaning and so should be given its normal everyday meaning.
That is, in this context, of large size or amount. DMs should note that this exception only applies if the
claimant and absent person have previously been members of the same household, notwithstanding that
that household may have been abroad and the intention must not be conditional.


Example 1


Blair is claiming SPC. He and his wife Isobel live in the same household. Isobel is involved in a road
accident and is admitted to hospital. She needs prolonged treatment and rehabilitation and is expected
to be in hospital about 14 months. The DM treats her as part of Blair's household during her absence.


Example 2


Angela is claiming SPC having recently returned from Italy where she had been living with her partner
Toni. Toni will come and join her in a months time. Angela and Toni are not members of the same
household (although they would be if Angela was claiming IS).

record.text:
Meaning of household

77102 Household has no specific legal meaning and so should be given its normal everyday meaning.

That is a domestic establishment containing the essentials of home life 1. Household may refer to people

held together by a particular kind of tie, even if temporarily separated 2. People living in one dwelling (for
example a house, flat or caravan) do not necessarily live together in the same household.


                                                          1 R(SB) 4/83; 2 Santos v. Santos [1972] All ER 246


Example


Andy and Aniza are estranged and continue to live in the same house. They do not financially support
each other or share domestic and social activities. One partner is reluctant to leave until a satisfactory
financial agreement has been reached with the other partner. They each have separate households.

record.text: A limited disregard for the residence condition of the Pension Credit severe-disability additional amount, not a finding that a person is absent from the household for every purpose. Assess normal residence separately. The captured DMG 78077 categories are: a person aged under 18; a person receiving source-defined “AA”, highest- or middle-rate DLA care, standard- or enhanced-rate PIP or ADP daily living, or AFIP; a person certified as blind or severely sight impaired by a consultant ophthalmologist or treated as such; a person living with the claimant to care for the claimant or partner who is engaged by a charitable or voluntary organisation which charges the claimant or partner for their services; that carer’s partner; and a source-defined qualifying young person, or a child for Child Benefit purposes. DMG 78008 limits treated blindness to 28 weeks after regained eyesight and no longer being certified. A voluntary organisation is non-profit and is not a public authority or local authority. Named young-person definitions have age, education, training, benefit-receipt and interruption conditions; neither education alone nor being under 20 is enough. DMG 78078(1) requires first joining the household to care for the claimant or partner, with the claimant or partner satisfying the additional-amount conditions immediately beforehand, and applies only for the first 12 weeks after joining. Its commercial-payment route concerns a person who is not a close relative: payment liability runs either from that person to the claimant or partner for occupation of their dwelling, or from the claimant or partner to that person for occupation of that person’s dwelling; it also covers membership of that person’s household. DMG 78079 requires legal liability and a payment broadly comparable to a lodger’s similar accommodation and facilities. The joint-occupation route requires co-ownership or joint liability to the same landlord, with its non-close-relative condition and the person’s-partner branch. The close-relative exception requires satisfying DMG 78078(3) or (4) as well as the timing condition: the claimant or partner’s co-ownership or joint liability must have arisen before 11 April 1988 or, if later, on or before first occupation; the note uses the right-to-occupy date, not a later moving-in date. Close relative has the captured legal, adoptive and half-sibling meanings. DMG 78080’s registered shared-lives route must retain the accommodation/support and commercial licence conditions and the exclusion where other people cannot be ignored; its completed example is not a general award rule or a current rate. Memo 02/25 paragraph 15 adds Pension Age Disability Payment to the ignored-person benefit list from 21 October 2024, separately from the memo’s claimant/partner and housing-deduction propositions. The dated statutory paragraph 2 also contains Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance wording requiring separate legal reconciliation; this concept does not consolidate it. Receipt conditions need the full DMG 78060 continuation: its partner-patient item must not be transferred automatically to a third person. Residence, receipt and component, age, care arrangements, relationship, liability and relevant dates remain unknown until evidenced. No staff question establishes these facts or that this component is payable.

record.text: Source-bounded navigation through DMG 78065–78076, separate from ignoring a person’s presence under 78077–78080 and from deciding whether partners remain one household. Normal residence is where a person usually lives: exceptional visits or absences are disregarded, and temporary absence does not itself change the normal home. DMG 78067 requires factual consideration of time, frequency, permanence, intentions, circumstances, degree of sharing, services, other accommodation and liabilities. An address, university term or overnight stay alone does not settle that assessment. Sharing only a bathroom, lavatory or communal area, or separate legal payment liabilities to the same landlord, has the captured sharing exceptions. Kitchen sharing can exist without entering or using it when personal items are stored or meals prepared there; merely passing through to a self-contained flat is different. DMG 78072–78075 require the contractual capacity and intention to create legal relations, an obligation for occupation from a recognised source of law, and the stipulated connection between non-payment and ending the licence or lease; another liability to a third party is not the same-landlord condition. Retain the England-and-Wales scope and presumption in the captured capacity passage rather than infer incapacity from a diagnosis. For an overnight carer, establish the separate address, actual use and frequency, postal address and Council Tax registration. All residence and contractual facts remain unknown until evidenced. A finding about this residence condition is not a finding of benefit entitlement, ignored-person status or continuing couple membership.

When does income become capital
84922 Where a claimant receives income, at a certain point that income becomes capital. This point is
reached when the period for which the income is paid has expired. So the DM should have regard to

receipts of income when calculating tariff income deemed to be generated from a claimant’s capital 1.


Example


Bill submits a claim for SPC on 21 August. He provides a bank statement dated 18 August showing a
balance of £12,335.46. If tariff income were calculated on this amount it would be £5.00 per week. Bill
also receives RP of £415.63 which is paid four weekly directly into this bank account. He last received a

payment on 17 August


to cover the period 17 August to 13 September. At the date of claim, as the period for which the RP was
paid has not yet expired, his capital should be reduced by the amount of his 4 weekly payment of RP. This
reduces his capital to £11,919.83 which produces a tariff income of £4.00 per week.

record.text:
Members of a multiple relationship
77116 There is no special rule to cover multiple relationships. If the claimant is


1. married to one but not all of the other members of the relationship - the DM should treat any
unmarried member as a claimant who has no partner


2. not married to any of the members - the DM should treat each member of the relationship as a
claimant who has no partner. This is because when a claimant has a relationship similar to marriage with
two or more people, none of them can form an unmarried couple.


Example 1


Alan, Bronwyn and Carol live in the same household but are not married to each other. Alan who is aged
65, claims SPC and states that he is in a multiple relationship with both Bronwyn and Carol. He is treated
as a claimant who has no partner and is awarded SPC as a person who has no partner. Bronwyn and Carol
are also treated as claimants who have no partner.

Example 2


Alan, Bronwyn and Carol live in the same household. Alan is married to Bronwyn but in his claim for SPC
states that he is also in a relationship with Carol. Alan is treated as a member of a couple with his wife
Bronwyn and is awarded SPC as a claimant who has a partner. Carol is treated as a claimant who has no
partner.

How to work out the amount of deemed weekly income

Total amount of capital
84921 The total amount of capital each person has is the total of the value of each item of actual capital
and notional capital that person has. The total amount of capital of claimants is


1. the total amount of their capital if they do not have a partner or


2. the total amount of their capital and the total amount of their partner’s capital if they have a partner 1.

record.label: Pension Credit household separation and care-home residence
record.scope: Frozen-source staff-question research. Source text is not current-law assurance and proposed meaning is not an official interpretation. Concept role: dwp:Circumstance.
record.text: DMG 77013 defines a couple; DMG 77102 explains household as a domestic establishment, not merely a building. Under DMG 77128, one partner entering a care home permanently is treated as no longer in the same household. Where both enter permanently, the decision maker must establish whether they remain one household on the facts. DMG 77129–77130 require reasonable independence and responsibility in running a domestic establishment; the seven factors are non-exhaustive and none is decisive alone. DMG 78089 says each may claim when household membership ends, not that an award automatically follows. Temporary absence is a separate branch.

record.scope: Frozen-source staff-question research. Source text is not current-law assurance and proposed meaning is not an official interpretation. Concept role: dwp:Applicability.
record.text: DMG 77035 distinguishes new claims from 15 May 2019 and continuity protection linked to Pension Credit or pension-age Housing Benefit on 14 May 2019. DMG 77140–77184 distinguish the mixed-age definition, Universal Credit interaction, excluded-partner exceptions and effective dates. The general exclusion is not the complete rule. DMG memo 04/24 paragraphs 15–17 add a protected mixed-age migration route from 8 June 2024: the specified protected couples sent a migration notice may reclaim pension-age Housing Benefit or claim Pension Credit within three months after the relevant UC or HB award ends. That route requires its stated prior entitlement and migration facts; it is not a general right for every mixed-age couple. Contemporary applicability, legislation and the ADM counterpart still require reconciliation.
